answer: Each agent identity rests on a jetty of locked collateral: registration posts a bond, and a public randomness beacon picks auditors who check that one payment key backs one name. To clone, an attacker must fund a separate bond and entry fee for every fake identity, and a single caught clone slashes the whole linked pool. The nadir of the attack's payoff arrives when rewards per honest agent sink below that per-clone cost, so mass registration burns capital instead of earning it.
